Agent.description: A coding agent, by the name `--agents` and a project's settings take.

AgentsLine.description:
What an `agents` line says, as the toggles have it.

`{"type": "named", "agents": ["claude"]}` in JSON: tagged as a task is,
with the agents beside the tag, since a variant holding a list has no
field of its own for them to be named by.

oneOf.description: `agents --yes <agent>...`: exactly these.

`agents remove --yes <agent>...`: none of these, every one the
project names, which is how a line asks for no agent at all, since
naming none is not one. The command refuses it, with its own reason.

AgentsLineSent.description:
What an `agents` line says, as the toggles have it.

`{"type": "named", "agents": ["claude"]}` in JSON: tagged as a task is,
with the agents beside the tag, since a variant holding a list has no
field of its own for them to be named by.

oneOf.description: `agents --yes <agent>...`: exactly these.

`agents remove --yes <agent>...`: none of these, every one the
project names, which is how a line asks for no agent at all, since
naming none is not one. The command refuses it, with its own reason.

Boxes.description:
How one entry in the registry stands with every offer ([`Offered`]):
what each of its boxes shows, told as the install screen tells it, by
[`install::survey`] and [`install::holding`], so the panel ticks the box
the screen ticks.

A box neither listed in `held` nor of a kind in `closed` is empty: the
project holds nothing of its name, and records no installation of it.
Only the boxes that are not are listed, a project holding a few of the
hundreds offered.

closed.description:
Each kind none of its boxes can be asked about, and why, by the code
a plan locks one by: every kind of an entry that opens no project,
and each a project has nowhere to put ([`install::receives`]), or
could not be surveyed for.

held.description:
Each box of a name it holds something of or records, kind by kind,
in the order of [`Snapshot::offers`].

Caution.description:
What a command line takes away, which a front end asks somebody to
confirm before it runs the line: what [`cautions`] reads off the parsed
command, as [`refused`] reads a refusal, so a line is asked about the
same way whatever task it came from, and by every front end.

One list, here, rather than one per front end: the panel holds no rules
(D-18), so which of its lines need a yes first is said with each preview
it is answered with, in these words, and a list in TypeScript would be a
second place for a command to be forgotten. The TUI asks its own
questions, worded for the row they are about, before it builds a task.

Only what takes something away, or writes over somebody's work: a line
that only adds, or that changes what is installed where its agents now
read, is shown before it runs and runs once asked. And never a dry run,
which a line of a command that takes `--yes` is without it: it takes
nothing away, and says what it would.

oneOf.description: `remove --yes`, at either level: the artifact deleted.

`uninstall`, every form of it, and `mindweaver remove --everywhere
--yes`, which uninstalls from every project first.
`unlink`, at either level.

`unload`, at either level: `unlink`'s twin, for a loaded workspace,
whose copies in the projects are left orphaned.

`--force`: on `install` and `uninstall`, and on `update` that is
told `--yes`.

Cell.description:
One box of a selection: whether `project` should hold what `reference`
names, as `origin` offers it.

`{"project": "alpha", "reference": "skill:deploy", "origin": "workspace",
"wanted": true}` in JSON, which the panel sends: the project by its entry
as the workspace's marker spells it, as a snapshot lists it, the artifact
as a command line names it, and the origin as `--from` takes it, which
every listing prints. A field it does not name is refused, as a task's
is.

wanted.description: Whether the project should hold it from there: ticked, or not.

CellSent.description:
One box of a selection: whether `project` should hold what `reference`
names, as `origin` offers it.

`{"project": "alpha", "reference": "skill:deploy", "origin": "workspace",
"wanted": true}` in JSON, which the panel sends: the project by its entry
as the workspace's marker spells it, as a snapshot lists it, the artifact
as a command line names it, and the origin as `--from` takes it, which
every listing prints. A field it does not name is refused, as a task's
is.

wanted.description: Whether the project should hold it from there: ticked, or not.

CliCode.description:
Every code the CLI gives of its own, for what went wrong: unique beside
core's and the local server's, and never renamed once given.

Closed.description: A kind none of a project's boxes of can be asked about, and why.

Confirm.description:
One thing a line of a task takes away, which the panel has somebody
confirm before it asks for the run: an item of a preview's `confirm`,
one for each [`Caution`] of each line ([`cautioned`]).

The words beside the word, so the panel says what a line takes in the
CLI's words rather than its own, and draws by the word alone.

line.description: Which of the preview's lines, by its place among them, from 0.

message.description: The same, said for whoever is asked.

Conflict.description:
Boxes of one name in one project that cannot all be as asked, and why:
none of them is planned, since which of them was meant is not something
to guess.

cells.description: Each box that clashes, as it was asked.

Contents.description: One file of an artifact, as a front end may show it.

file.description:
The file, as it was asked for: a route from the artifact's folder,
`/` separated, or a rule's own file name.

hash.description:
The SHA-256 of what it holds ([`hash::bytes`]), when it was read
whole: none for one larger than [`CAP`], which never is.

What `edit --if-unchanged` takes, so a front end that changes the
file holds the change to what it read, and is refused when somebody
changed it since (`edit_stale`). Hashed here, of the bytes the text
was read from, rather than by the front end from the text: one
recipe for every hash of a file, and a text a browser hashed could
be told apart from the file by nothing but a line ending.

manifest.description:
What it declares and says, cut as core reads it, when it is the file
the artifact is read from (a skill's `SKILL.md`, a rule's own file)
and its text was read; none for any other file, whose front matter
no agent reads as such.

text.description:
What it says, when it is UTF-8 text no larger than [`CAP`]; none
otherwise, and [`withheld`](Self::withheld) says why.

withheld.description: Why there is no text, when there is none.

CoreCode.description: Every code core gives, for what went wrong: unique across core, and never renamed once given.

Crumb.description: One folder on the way down to the one listed.

name.description: Its name, or the root's path for the root, which has none.

Declaration.description: One key of an artifact's front matter, and what it is given.

value.description:
A string as it is; anything else, a list or a mapping, a number or
nothing, as YAML writes it, so a value is shown whatever its shape
rather than only those the format defines.

Directory.description: Where a holder keeps one kind.

path.description:
A route from the holder, `/` separated, or the path itself when no
route leads there.

Does.description: What an update does with one installation.

Draft.description:
An artifact a command is about to write, as the panel asks core to judge
it ([`Query::Validate`]): tagged as a query is, `{"type": "add", ...}`.

oneOf.description:
What `add` would write, by the fields an `add` task carries: a
template by its name, as `--template` takes it.

What `edit --contents` would write into the artifact `reference`
names, `kind:name`, given `text` whole: its `SKILL.md`, or a rule's
file.

Drafted.description:
What `POST /api/v1/validate` is sent: a draft, and what it would be
written in ([`Query::Validate`]).

Entry.description:
One line of the action log.

What it serializes to is a contract, as a status report's is: each field
by its name, and the two that can quote a URL as a [`Redacted`], which
holds none. A row an older build wrote before the scrub still holds one
in the file until a command that writes opens the ledger, and is
redacted as it is read ([`history`](LedgerStore::history)).

at.description: When it happened, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

detail.description: What it said, successful or not, with every URL in it [`redacted`].

target.description: What the action was about: a URL, a name. A URL is [`redacted`].

Event.description:
One thing the panel is told.

Tagged by its name in snake_case beside its fields, as a task and a
query are: `{"type": "changed", "scopes": [...]}`.

oneOf.description:
Something a backend watches changed on disk, so what the panel shows
of each scope may be out of date: one event for every change the
watcher took in together, each scope once, in the backend's words.
A task's lines started to run on the writer thread.
They stopped, however that went: the reply to the run says how.

The backend acts on something else since ([`Backend::switch`]),
and what it names is watched: everything is to be asked for again,
and nothing shown before kept, since it was of what it acted on
before. Told on the writer thread, once the switch is taken, to
every subscriber, the tab that asked for it among them
([`Events::switched`]), with how many switches were taken since the
bus was made, this one counted.

[`Backend::switch`]: crate::Backend::switch

The subscriber may have missed something: it has just connected, or
it fell behind. Everything is to be asked for again.

With how many switches were taken since the bus was made, as the
latest [`Switched`](Event::Switched) said: a subscriber that missed
one, a tab whose stream was let go while it was hidden or one that
fell behind, learns it from a count other than the one it heard last,
and lets go of what it shows of what the backend acted on before as
it would on hearing `Switched`. A count rather than a word that a
switch happened, which only a bus that knew what each subscriber had
heard could say.

Every path the backend named is watched, so a change to one arrives
as [`Changed`](Event::Changed).

Not every one is, so a change there arrives as nothing, and what the
panel shows is refreshed by hand: the system's limit on watches was
reached, or a watch could not be set up at all.

Files.description: Every file and folder of an artifact, as a front end may list them.

entries.description:
Each file and folder it holds, a folder before what it holds and
each folder's in the order of their names: a rule's one file alone.

manifest.description:
The file it is read from, as [`Contents`] takes it: a skill's
`SKILL.md`, or a rule's own file name. Said rather than left to a
front end, which would otherwise spell where each kind keeps what
it says.

truncated.description: Whether it holds more than [`FILES_CAP`], which `entries` stops at.

Folder.description: One folder directly inside the one listed.

linked.description:
Whether the workspace links it, by the path an entry leads to, as
`mindweaver link` would tell.

path.description: Where it is, absolute, as a request names it to list it in turn.

symlink.description:
Whether it is a link to a folder rather than a folder: listed and
opened as one all the same.

FolderIs.description:
What a folder is, the strongest of what it holds: a mind project, a
weaver workspace, a git repository, or any other folder.

Folders.description:
One folder and the folders directly inside it, as a front end may offer
them to be chosen.

failures.description:
What it could not read or name, each with its code
([`BrowseFailure`]): a subfolder whose type will not read, or whose
path no request could send back, a hidden one only when hidden
ones are asked for.

folders.description:
Its subfolders, in the order of their names, hidden ones only when
asked for, and no more than [`FOLDERS_CAP`].

hidden.description:
How many of its subfolders are hidden, their names starting with a
`.`, listed or not: what asking for them would list, the bound
aside.

home.description:
The home the front end was given, normalized, as a folder a request
may name, for a way back to it: none when there is none, or when it
is no such path ([`policy::path`]).

is.description: What it is itself, so it can be chosen as one of its subfolders can.

path.description: The folder listed, absolute, as it was asked for.

trail.description:
Each folder from the root down to it, it last: what a front end
offers to go up by, each by the path it is asked for by.

truncated.description:
Whether it holds more subfolders than [`FOLDERS_CAP`], which
`folders` stops at.

Found.description:
A directory a workspace could manage.

What it serializes to is a contract, as a status report's is: each field
by its name. The panel reads it in what a scan it asks for is answered
with, so it says its TypeScript too.

agent_files.description:
Each name at its root an agent reads something from
([`Agent::reads_at_root`], of every agent), in name order: what makes
a repository's reason [`Reason::Agents`], and listed for a mind
project too, which can hold them as well. Looked at, never followed
or read: a link there counts as what it is called.

id.description:
The id its settings name it by (D-09), whatever it is called and
wherever it is: none for a git repository that is not a project yet,
for a project a `mind.toml` still marks, which has none, and for one
whose marker would not open, which is a failure beside it.

linked.description: Whether the workspace links it already.

mind.description:
A mind project already, rather than a git repository that is not one
yet and would need `mind init` before it can be linked.

moved.description:
The entry it moved from, when it is not linked and holds the id the
workspace's ledger last saw at an entry where no project is any more
([`MindProject::is_vacant`]): spelled as `route` is, so `mindweaver
relink <moved> <route>` run there follows it. None otherwise, and for
an id another directory holds too, which is a copy rather than a
move.

reason.description: Why it is worth linking: the strongest of what it holds.

route.description:
What `mindweaver link` would be given for it, run where the request
spells routes from: the route from there, `/` separated, when it is
inside, and its path otherwise.

Health.description: How a project stands as a whole.

Held.description: One artifact a holder holds, and how it stands there.

agents.description:
The agents among its project's that read a copy of it, in report
order.

issues.description:
Everything `validate` says of it, warnings included, each saying
whether it is one.

origin.description: Where what was installed came from, as `--from` takes it.

state.description:
How its name stands in its project, as `status` says; none for the
library's own, which are no project's. Only a copy that reads has a
standing, so beside an [`unread`](Self::unread) one it is that of a
copy of the name elsewhere, in an agent's folder, and none when
there is no such copy.

summary.description:
The one line a listing shows; none for one whose file does not read,
and for an install nothing of which is found.

targets.description:
Where it is held, as routes from its holder, `/` separated, in path
order: each copy discovery found, the one whose file does not read
among them, and each place the ledger records putting one, found or
not.

unread.description:
The copy whose file does not read, when one does not, and why.
Listed all the same, by the name its place gives it, because a file
that does not read is the one most in need of opening.

HeldBox.description:
A box of an offer whose name a project holds something of, or records
an installation of: how the name stands, and whether the box is ticked.

state.description:
How the name stands in the project, as every offer of it stands
([`State::of_standing`]): never `authored`, which no offer is.

ticked.description:
Whether the box is ticked ([`install::holding`]): the offer the
installation came from, every offer of a name somebody's copy holds,
and none of one whose every copy has gone, for ticking it to put
them back.

Holder.description:
Which level a task runs at: what holds the artifacts it is about.

`{"type": "project", "entry": "alpha"}` in JSON, or `{"type":
"workspace"}`: the shape a task's own variants have, which a variant
holding one string cannot take inside the object the tag is in.

oneOf.description: The workspace, for its own artifacts: `mindweaver <cmd>`.

A project, by its entry: `mind -C <entry> <cmd>`, or `mind <cmd>` for
the one at the root the commands run from.

A project whose own workspace is not the one on screen, by its entry:
`mind -W . -C <entry> <cmd>`, which names the one on screen, so a
change drops that workspace's record and an add takes its templates.

Still the project's command rather than `mindweaver <cmd> -p <entry>`,
which would consult the same workspace: a project's row teaches the
project's command, at every row alike, and `-W` only where leaving
it out would consult another.

HolderSent.description:
Which level a task runs at: what holds the artifacts it is about.

`{"type": "project", "entry": "alpha"}` in JSON, or `{"type":
"workspace"}`: the shape a task's own variants have, which a variant
holding one string cannot take inside the object the tag is in.

oneOf.description: The workspace, for its own artifacts: `mindweaver <cmd>`.

A project, by its entry: `mind -C <entry> <cmd>`, or `mind <cmd>` for
the one at the root the commands run from.

A project whose own workspace is not the one on screen, by its entry:
`mind -W . -C <entry> <cmd>`, which names the one on screen, so a
change drops that workspace's record and an add takes its templates.

Still the project's command rather than `mindweaver <cmd> -p <entry>`,
which would consult the same workspace: a project's row teaches the
project's command, at every row alike, and `-W` only where leaving
it out would consult another.

Judged.description:
What core says of a draft: what `validate` would say of it once written,
and why the command writing it would write nothing, when it would.

Each field by its name, a contract once a front end reads it, as a
report's are.

issues.description:
Everything `validate` would say of the artifact as it would be
written, warnings included, in its words: none when what would be
written cannot be told.

refused.description:
Why the command would write nothing, by the code and in the words it
would refuse with; none when it would write.

Kind.description: A kind of artifact, by the word a command line takes for it.

KindTargets.description: The folders a project's settings install one kind in.

folders.description: Each folder as the settings spell it, `/` separated.

KnownHere.description:
A workspace this machine knows, as `mindweaver workspaces` lists it, with
how the workspace a snapshot is of stands with it: whether it loads it,
and whether it could.

Beside the row rather than in it, as a shelf row's origin is
([`Shelved`]): the row is the machine's list, the same whichever
workspace asks, and what one of them loads is nothing that list says.
Told here rather than by a front end from `in_use`, `stale` and
[`Snapshot::loaded`], whose paths it would compare itself: two spellings
of one folder are one workspace, which only a comparison of where each
leads tells.

default.description:
The default workspace, in home: listed for being the default,
whatever its own `known` says.

in_use.description: The one in use where the list was asked for, as `resolve` chose it.

loadable.description:
Whether this workspace can load it: it opens, it is not this one,
this one loads it by no spelling yet, and its path is text a command
line can hold. What a front end offers to load, by its `path`, which
`mindweaver load` is given as it is.

loaded_as.description:
The entry this workspace loads it by, when it loads it, as
[`LoadedWorkspace::entry`] spells it: what `mindweaver unload` is given.
The first, when it loads it by more than one spelling.

name.description:
What its marker calls it; none for one that would not open, which has
no marker to read.

projects.description:
How many projects it links, each directory once, stale ones among
them: its own count, which says which of several weavers is which.

remembered.description:
Whether the default workspace's `known` names it, which is what
`mindweaver workspaces forget` takes out. False for the default itself,
and for the one in use when nothing remembers it.

stale.description:
Why it would not open, when it would not: listed rather than left
out, since a workspace that has gone is the one somebody has to find
to forget it.

Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as an error's
message is in a [`Said`](crate::code::Said): a marker that does not
parse is quoted in its own words, a source's URL among them perhaps,
and whoever wrote that file is no promise that it holds no
credential.

stale_projects.description: How many of those would not open.

Library.description: The workspace's own artifacts, held as a project holds its own.

artifacts.description:
Each of its own, by kind and then name: no project's, so none
stands in a state, and nothing is installed into them.

directories.description: Where it keeps each kind, as a route from the workspace's root.

failures.description:
What could not be read in it and is no artifact's: a folder that
cannot be listed, its templates.

holders.description:
Each project its registry links that holds a copy of one of its own,
in the order of `artifacts`, then of the registry.

origin.description:
What `--from` takes for each of its own, and what an install of one
records as its origin: so a front end names it in a command line by
core's word rather than by one of its own that core could spell
differently.

LibraryHolder.description:
A project holding a copy of one of the workspace's own: one whose install
the ledger tells came from it ([`install::from_the_library`]), the rule
`mindweaver remove --everywhere` takes the copies it removes by.

Told here rather than by a front end comparing a copy's
[`origin`](Held::origin) with [`Library::origin`], which would be a
rule of its own, and a different one: a record from before origins were
kept names none, and is a copy of one of the workspace's own all the
same while no workspace it loads offers that name.

entry.description:
The project, as its registry entry spells it ([`Project::entry`]):
its artifact of that kind and name is the copy. Each entry that
spells one directory is a holder of its own, as each is a project
of the snapshot's.

kind.description: The one of the workspace's own it holds a copy of.

Listed.description: One file or folder of an artifact.

folder.description: Whether it is a folder, whose files are listed after it.

path.description:
Its route from the artifact's folder, `/` separated, as [`Contents`]
takes it; a rule's own file name. One whose name no route spells is
refused (`contents_name_unfit`) and listed by that name as near as
UTF-8 writes it, which another entry's can match: a refused entry is
shown, never asked for.

refused.description:
Why it is not followed, when it is not: a link leading out of the
holder, or back into a folder it is in, or something that does not
read. Listed all the same, since somebody looking for why a skill
misbehaves is looking for exactly that.

size.description:
How many bytes a file holds; none for a folder, and for one not
followed.

LoadedWorkspace.description: A workspace another one loads, and how much of its own it offers.

entry.description: The entry as the marker spells it: what `mindweaver unload` is given.

error.description: Why it would not open, when it would not.

name.description: Its name; none for one that would not open.

offers.description:
How many of its own it offers to install, counted from what the
install machinery offers, so the number is what an install shows. A
second spelling of one workspace offers what the first does.

origin.description:
What `--from` takes for what it offers, and what an install of one
of them records as its origin: the first spelling's, for a second
spelling of one workspace, as its offers are.

path.description: Where it points: what `mind unload` is given, from a project.

Locked.description:
A box whose change is not made, and why, by the code the change would be
refused with: `foreign` and `edited` as an install or an uninstall gives
them ([`Refused`]), or the error asking the project for it gave.

Manifest.description:
The file an artifact is read from, cut at its front matter as core cuts
it: what a front end shows as a table of what it declares above the
markdown it renders.

Cut here rather than by a front end from [`Contents::text`], since where
front matter ends, and whether a rule's fences hold any, are rules
([`frontmatter::split`], [`RuleManifest::read`]): a panel cutting it
itself could show as declared what every agent reads as content.

body.description:
What follows the front matter, as an agent reads it: the whole file
when no front matter is read.

front_matter.description:
Each key at the top of its front matter, in the order written, every
one the format does not define among them; none when it has none
core reads: no fences, fences that never close, or a block that is
no YAML mapping.

Mark.description:
One directory a front end marked, by the path a command is given, with
what to do to it: what [`Task::Marks`] holds, and [`Task::minds`] builds
a batch from. `{"path": "/home/you/blog", "change": "link"}` in JSON.

MarkSent.description:
One directory a front end marked, by the path a command is given, with
what to do to it: what [`Task::Marks`] holds, and [`Task::minds`] builds
a batch from. `{"path": "/home/you/blog", "change": "link"}` in JSON.

MarkerFile.description: The file inside `.mind` a project's marker is read from.

MindsChange.description:
What one directory's mark on the minds screen asks of the workspace, when
it differs from how the directory started: what [`Task::minds`] is built
from. By its name in snake_case in JSON: `"init_and_link"`.

oneOf.description:
`mind init` in it, then link it: a repository that is not a mind
project yet.

Missed.description:
One artifact a project received that some of its agents read nowhere,
and those agents.

agents.description:
The agents among the project's that read it nowhere, in report
order. Never empty.

Offered.description:
One thing there is to install, from one place: a row of the install
screen turned round by artifact, and of the panel's matrix (#79).

Told by core's own list of what an install offers ([`install::survey`]),
rather than put together by a front end from the library, the shelf and
the loads: only that list leaves out a name no copy can be filed under,
and reads what each loaded workspace offers, which nothing else in a
snapshot lists.

origin.description:
Where it is offered from, as `--from` takes it and an install of it
records it: what a box of it names its offer by.

summary.description: The one line a listing shows.

Outcome.description: What running a task's lines produced.

ok.description: Whether every line ran and found everything in order.

runs.description:
Each line that ran, in order: up to the first that failed, for a task
whose lines lean on each other ([`Task::chained`]).

Pending.description: One installation an update says something of.

copies.description:
The copies that names, each a route from the project, `/`
separated: put back, written over or left.

does.description: What an update does with it.

forced.description:
Whether a change reaches it only forced: a copy changed since it was
installed, which an update not forced leaves alone and, once nothing
offers it any more, an uninstall not forced leaves too. Said here so
a front end sends `--force` by core's word, rather than telling from
the state, the step, or both, which of core's refusals its change
would meet.

left.description:
Why an update leaves it as the project holds it, when it does
([`Left`]).

origin.description:
Where it came from, as `--from` takes it: none for a record from
before origins were kept.

state.description: How it stands, as `status` says it.

Place.description: Which of the three places offers something to install.

Planned.description:
What a selection the panel asked to plan amounts to ([`Query::Plan`]):
core's plan of it ([`install::Plan`]), each change in it the task that
runs it.

Tasks rather than core's changes, so the panel sends back what it was
handed, never a task it puts together itself: the `install` and
`uninstall` tasks, each a project by the entry its box named it by, which
the backend turns into the folder the registry resolves as it does any
task's. Sent as one `apply_install`, as the install screen applies its

locked.description:

tasks.description:

confirm.description:

item for each thing a line takes away; none for a task the panel
runs once it is asked to.

path's scope is: which lines take something away is a rule of the
front end's, and so are the words for it. Said where the lines are,
so the panel is told it of the very lines it shows, rather than
asking a second time about a disk that may have changed between.

asked anybody is run, as a shell runs the line typed into it, since

lines.description: The command lines, each as somebody would type it.

agents.description:

directories.description: Where it authors each kind, as a route from it.

entry.description:

failures.description:

misplaced.description: Each folder its settings name in `targets` that no install uses.

missed.description: Each rule it received that some of its agents read nowhere.

name.description: What its marker calls it; none for an entry that opens no project.

settings.description:

stale.description:

tally.description: How many of them are of each kind, and stand in each state.

templates.description: What `mind add --template` can start from in it.

unreached.description:

Task.description:
Work a front end asked for, as the command it is.

In JSON, what the panel sends to be run, each variant is an object
tagged by its name in snake_case, its fields beside the tag: `{"type":
"link", "path": "beta"}`. Tagged inside the object rather than around
it, so a task reads as one flat record, the shape TypeScript tells a
union apart by. A field a task with fields does not have is refused
rather than passed over, as one its holder or its agents line does not
have is: a task is a write, and one sent with a field misspelled would
run without it. Each name is a contract once a front end sends it, as a
report's is, so a test pins every one.

`mindweaver link <path>`.

rest, by the one function that says so, and the same marks make the

folder alike, and the same batch folder for folder inside the

policy takes, and the minds screen by its route from the root.
[`Minds`](Task::Minds) taken from a
browser was the other way, which would hold the panel to spelling

use marked, to read.

<kind>` when no folder is named: what the targets form amounts to.

agents.description: The agents to name, when they change.

share.description: The share mode, when it or `edit_tracked` changes.

oneOf.description:
What a project's toggles amount to, turned from `was`, what its
settings say, to `now`, what the toggles say: the
[`Settings`](Task::Settings) task [`Task::settings`] builds, whose
lines these are, as the TUI's toggles' are.

How the panel changes a project's agents and share mode: it sends
the toggles as they stand, never the lines' agents, so the order a
project names them in, and what unticking every one asks, is said by
the one function, never again in TypeScript. `was` is what the
panel read in the snapshot, as the TUI's is what it read when the
form opened: each line names the agents and the mode outright, so a
`was` the disk has moved on from changes which lines run, never what
a line sets.

`… update --yes [<kind:name>]`: what is installed in a project, or
the one artifact named, brought up to date and put back where a copy
has gone; `mindweaver update --all --yes [<kind:name>]` for the
workspace's own row, in every project it links. With `force`, `--yes

which the line is then asked about for ([`Caution::Forces`]).

offer into each project named, by what picks it out
([`WeaverWorkspace::naming`]), from the place `from` names when it
names one.

the root, never a project's name, though `-p` takes one: a value
that starts with a dash reaches `-p` behind a `./` (`directory`),

path, but is no longer a name `pick` would match. `-p=-odd`, which

back out of each project named, whichever place its copy came from,
each named as an install's are, by what `naming` gives. With
`force`, `--force`, taking out a copy changed since it was installed
too, which the line is then asked about for ([`Caution::Forces`]):
never from the install screen, whose marks leave an edit to a command
line, and from the panel only for the copy core says needs it.

nothing offers any more where it came from, taken back out of it;

row, out of every project it links, as an update reaches them. Never
forced: one changed since it was installed is left, every copy of it,
for a command line that says `--force` once somebody has looked.

the project's agents' folders brought into the workspace's library,
its copies recorded as installed from there: asked about before it
gets here, which is what the `--yes` says. The project is named as an
install's are, by what `naming` gives.

links moved from an older marker, a `mind.toml` or a
`settings.json`, to a `settings.toml`, what the workspace records of
it carried along; without `yes`, the dry run, which writes nothing
and says what would move. The project is named as an install's are,
by what `naming` gives.

The workspace's command, as an install's is, so what it carries is
what the workspace on screen records: `mind migrate` in the project
finds a workspace by walking up, which misses one linking the
project from beside it. The agents and the share mode are left to
the command, every agent and shared for a `mind.toml`, as a project
committed by design was, and what a `settings.json` names for one,

Open the install screen, which is what `mindweaver install` opens.

info.description:
The HTTP API `mindweaver ui` serves, for scripts and tools on this machine as much as for the web panel, its first client. A read is a GET naming what it reads in its parameters, and a read that takes a structure a POST that changes nothing; every change is a task, the command lines it is, previewed and then run, so the API does nothing the command line cannot. A script that did not start the panel finds where the API is and its token in the file `mindweaver ui --token-file` writes. A route, a parameter or a field once served is a contract: dropping or renaming one, or changing what it holds, moves the API to `/api/v2`, and adding one does not, so an answer's schema leaves room for a field it does not name. Written from the Rust that serves it, never by hand.

Served on 127.0.0.1 alone, at the port the system chose unless one was named, every route behind the launch token, as a Bearer token or as the cookie the launch link sets. Every answer that is no success is a `Refused`, `{"code", "error"}`, its code the word a script acts on and its error the words a person reads: a path under `/api` no route names, of another version or of none, is a 404 of `unknown_route`. Every answer under `/api` carries `Cache-Control: no-store`, and none grants another origin the right to read it.
